compsognathus:eswiki:12.title: Compsognathus longipes (Plumas y la conexión con las aves)

facts.statement: The genus Compsognathus was originally described by Edward Drinker Cope in 1875.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Cope, 1875

facts.statement: The genus name Compsognathus was coined by Johann A. Wagner in 1859.
facts.quote: authority: Wagner, 1859

facts.statement: Compsognathus longipes is the type species of the genus Compsognathus.
facts.quote: type_species: Compsognathus longipes

facts.statement: Compsognathus corallestris was proposed as a synonym of Compsognathus longipes by Bidar and colleagues in 1972.
facts.quote: synonyms: * Compsognathus corallestrisBidar et al., 1972

facts.statement: Compsognathus longipes could grow to approximately the size of a chicken.
facts.quote: Members of its single species Compsognathus longipes could grow to around the size of a chicken.

facts.statement: Paleontologists have found two well-preserved Compsognathus fossils, one in Germany in the 1850s and another in France discovered more than a century later.
facts.quote: Paleontologists have found two well-preserved fossils, one in Germany in the 1850s and the second in France more than a century later.

facts.statement: The German Compsognathus specimen is now believed to be a juvenile, which explains why it is often described as chicken-sized.
facts.quote: Many presentations still describe Compsognathus as "chicken-sized" dinosaurs because of the size of the German specimen, which is now believed to be a juvenile.

facts.statement: The diet of Compsognathus longipes is known with certainty from the remains of small, agile lizards preserved in the bellies of both specimens.
facts.quote: Compsognathus longipes is one of the few dinosaur species whose diet is known with certainty: the remains of small, agile lizards are preserved in the bellies of both specimens.

facts.statement: Until the 1990s, Compsognathus was considered the smallest-known non-avialan dinosaur and was incorrectly labeled as the closest relative of Archaeopteryx.
facts.quote: Until the 1990s, it was the smallest-known non-avialan dinosaur, with the preceding centuries incorrectly labelling it as the closest relative of Archaeopteryx.

facts.statement: The German Compsognathus specimen (BSP AS I 563) comes from limestone deposits in Bavaria and was part of the collection of Joseph Oberndorfer.
facts.quote: The German specimen (specimen number BSP AS I 563) stems from limestone deposits in Bavaria and was part of the collection of physician and fossil collector Joseph Oberndorfer.

facts.statement: Johann A. Wagner coined the name Compsognathus longipes in 1859 after receiving the specimen from Joseph Oberndorfer.
facts.quote: Oberndorfer lent the specimen to paleontologist Johann A. Wagner, who published a brief discussion in 1859, where he coined the name Compsognathus longipes.

facts.statement: Johann A. Wagner published a more detailed description of Compsognathus in 1861.
facts.quote: He published a more detailed description in 1861.

facts.statement: During the Jurassic, the region where the German Compsognathus fossils were found was part of the Solnhofen archipelago.
facts.quote: In the Jurassic, the region was part of the Solnhofen archipelago.

facts.statement: J.G. Baur removed the right ankle of the German Compsognathus specimen for study, but the part was subsequently lost.
facts.quote: The German paleontologist J.G. Baur, who worked as an assistant of Marsh, removed the right ankle from the slab for illustration and study; this removed part got lost since.

facts.statement: John Ostrom concluded that the German Compsognathus specimen likely belongs to an immature individual.
facts.quote: He also concluded that the German specimen likely belongs to an immature individual.

facts.statement: The larger French Compsognathus specimen (Y85R M4M) was discovered around 1971 in the Portlandian lithographic limestone of Canjuers near Nice.
facts.quote: The larger French specimen (Y85R M4M) was discovered in around 1971 in the Portlandian lithographic limestone of Canjuers near Nice.

facts.statement: The collection containing the French Compsognathus specimen was sold to the National Museum of Natural History in Paris in 1983.
facts.quote: The collection, including the Compsognathus specimen, was sold to the National Museum of Natural History in Paris in 1983.

facts.statement: Alain Bidar and Gérard Thomel announced the French Compsognathus find as a separate species, Compsognathus corallestris, in a 1972 description.
facts.quote: Alain Bidar and Gérard Thomel, in a brief 1972 description, announced the new find under a separate species, Compsognathus corallestris.

facts.statement: John Ostrom, Jean-Guy Michard, and others later relabeled the French specimen as Compsognathus longipes.
facts.quote: Ostrom, Jean-Guy Michard and others have since relabeled it as another example of Compsognathus longipes.

facts.statement: Jens Zinke labeled forty-nine teeth from Portugal as Compsognathus sp. because they had serrations on the front edge and were not identical to those of Compsognathus longipes.
facts.quote: Zinke found that these teeth are not identical to those of Compsognathus longipes, having serrations on the front edge, and thus labeled the teeth as Compsognathus sp. (of unknown species).

facts.statement: The German specimen of Compsognathus was estimated to be between 70 and 75 centimeters tall and 89 centimeters long, while the French specimen was estimated to be between 1.25 and 1.4 meters long.
facts.quote: The German specimen was estimated to be 70–75 cm and 89 cm in length by separate authors, while the larger French specimen was estimated at 1.25 m and 1.4 m in length.

facts.statement: The German specimen of Compsognathus was estimated to weigh between 0.32 and 0.58 kilograms, while the French specimen was estimated to weigh between 2.5 and 3.5 kilograms.
facts.quote: The German specimen was estimated to have weighed 0.32 kg and 0.58 kg, and the French specimen 2.5 kg and 3.5 kg.

facts.statement: Compsognathus were small, bipedal animals that used their long legs and long tails for balance while moving.
facts.quote: Compsognathus were small, bipedal animals with long legs and longer tails, which they used for balance during locomotion.

facts.statement: Compsognathus had small, pointed teeth suited for eating small vertebrates and possibly insects.
facts.quote: The teeth were small and pointed, suited for its diet of small vertebrates and possibly other small animals, such as insects.

facts.statement: Compsognathids were unique among theropods for having tooth crowns that curved backward at two-thirds of their height with straight mid-parts and expanded bases.
facts.quote: Compsognathids were unique among theropods in having tooth crowns that curved backwards at two thirds of their height, while their mid-parts were straight; also, the crowns had expanded bases.

facts.statement: The number of digits on the hand of Compsognathus has been a source of debate among scientists.
facts.quote: The number of digits on the hand of Compsognathus has been a source of debate.

facts.statement: A 2022 review interprets the skin impressions on the Compsognathus tail as aberrant bony growths rather than scales, noting they are texturally and mineralogically indistinguishable from the fossilized vertebrae.
facts.quote: A 2022 review of non-feather integument of non-avialan theropods interprets these structures as aberrant bony growths rather than scales, as the structures are "texturally and mineralogically indistinguishable" from the rest of the fossilized vertebrae.

facts.statement: Compsognathus was originally classified as a lizard, but its dinosaurian affinities were first noted by Gegenbaur, Cope, and Huxley between 1863 and 1868.
facts.quote: Originally classified as a lizard, the dinosaurian affinities of Compsognathus were first noted by Gegenbaur, Cope, and Huxley between 1863 and 1868.

facts.statement: Friedrich von Huene erected the infraorder Coelurosauria in 1914, which includes the Compsognathidae among other families of small theropods, and this classification has remained in use since.
facts.quote: Friedrich von Huene, in 1914, erected the new infraorder Coelurosauria, which includes the Compsognathidae amongst other families of small theropods; this classification remained in use since.

facts.statement: The Compsognathidae, the group containing Compsognathus, lived during the late Jurassic and early Cretaceous periods in China, Europe, and South America.
facts.quote: The Compsognathidae are a group of mostly small dinosaurs from the late Jurassic and early Cretaceous periods of China, Europe and South America.

facts.statement: A 2001 study by Bruce Rothschild and others examined nine foot bones of Compsognathus for stress fractures but found none.
facts.quote: In a 2001 study conducted by Bruce Rothschild and other paleontologists, nine foot bones referred to Compsognathus were examined for signs of stress fracture, but none were found.

facts.statement: Bidar and colleagues argued in 1972 that the French specimen of Compsognathus had webbed hands that would have looked like flippers in life.
facts.quote: Bidar and colleagues, in their 1972 description of the French specimen, argued that this specimen had webbed hands which would look like flippers in life.

facts.statement: Ostrom debunked the hypothesis of webbed hands in Compsognathus, noting the forelimb was poorly preserved and the wrinkles likely represented sedimentary structures unrelated to the fossil.
facts.quote: Ostrom debunked this hypothesis, noting that the forelimb of the French specimen is poorly preserved, and that the wrinkles extend well beyond the skeleton and thus are likely sedimentary structures unrelated to the fossil.

facts.statement: Compsognathus preyed on small vertebrates, as evidenced by lizard remains found in the stomach of a German specimen.
facts.quote: The remains of a lizard in the German specimen's thoracic cavity show that Compsognathus preyed on small vertebrates.

facts.statement: The lizard found in the stomach of the German Compsognathus specimen was identified as a new species named Schoenesmahl dyspepsia.
facts.quote: Conrad made the lizard found in the thoracic cavity of the German specimen of Compsognathus the holotype of a new species Schoenesmahl dyspepsia.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Compsognathus dismembered its prey with its hands and teeth before swallowing the pieces whole, a behavior similar to modern birds of prey.
facts.quote: The lizard is in several pieces, indicating that the Compsognathus must have dismembered it while restraining it with its hands and teeth, and then swallowed the remains whole; a similar strategy is used by modern predatory birds.

facts.statement: The stomach contents of the French Compsognathus specimen consist of unidentified lizards or sphenodontids.
facts.quote: The French specimen's gastric contents consist of unidentified lizards or sphenodontids.

facts.statement: In 1993, Peter Griffiths interpreted circular irregularities on the German Compsognathus slab as immature eggs.
facts.quote: Peter Griffiths interpreted them as immature eggs in 1993.

facts.statement: Later researchers doubt the identification of the circular irregularities as Compsognathus eggs because they were found outside the animal's body cavity.
facts.quote: However, later researchers have doubted their connection to the genus because they were found outside the body cavity of the animal.

facts.statement: In 1964, Karl Werner Barthel proposed that the circular marks on the fossil were gas bubbles formed by the decomposition of the carcass.
facts.quote: In 1964 German geologist Karl Werner Barthel had explained the discs as gas bubbles formed in the sediment because of the putrefaction of the carcass.

facts.statement: A 2007 computer model estimated that Compsognathus could reach a maximum speed of 17.8 m/s.
facts.quote: In 2007, William Sellers and Phillip Manning estimated a maximum speed of 17.8 m/s based on a computer model of the skeleton and muscles.

facts.statement: Compsognathus specimens from Germany and France were found in lagoons situated between beaches and coral reefs on Jurassic European islands.
facts.quote: Both the German and French areas where Compsognathus specimens have been preserved were lagoons situated between the beaches and coral reefs of the Jurassic European islands in the Tethys Sea.

facts.statement: No other dinosaur fossils have been found with Compsognathus, suggesting it may have been the top land predator on its islands.
facts.quote: No other dinosaur has been found in association with Compsognathus, indicating that these little dinosaurs might in fact have been the top land predator in these islands.

facts.statement: In 2012, Reisdorf and Wuttke speculated about the events leading to the death and burial of the German Compsognathus specimen.
facts.quote: Reisdorf and Wuttke, in 2012, speculated about the events that lead to the death and transportation of the specimen to its place of burial.

facts.statement: The German Compsognathus specimen is highly articulated, with disarticulation only seen in the skull, hands, cervical ribs, and gastralia.
facts.quote: The German specimen was preserved with a high degree of articulation—only the skull, hands, cervical ribs and gastralia show disarticulation.

facts.statement: In 1918, physician Moodie hypothesized that the characteristic death pose of Compsognathus resulted from opisthotonus, or death throes causing muscle stiffening.
facts.quote: The physician Moodie, in 1918, suggested that the death pose in Compsognathus and similar fossils was the result of an opisthotonus—death throes causing spastic stiffening of the back musculature—while the animal was dying.

facts.statement: In 1991, Peter Wellnhofer argued that the death pose of Compsognathus was caused by the elastic pull of ligaments released after death.
facts.quote: Peter Wellnhofer, in 1991, argued that death poses resulted from the elastic pull of the ligaments, which are released after death.

facts.statement: In 2007, Cynthia Faux and Kevin Padian supported the hypothesis that the death pose of Compsognathus was caused by opisthotonus.
facts.quote: The veterinarian Cynthia Faux and the paleontologist Kevin Padian, in a 2007 study that gained much attention, supported the original opisthotonus hypothesis of Moodie.

facts.statement: Reisdorf and Wuttke concluded that the death posture of Compsognathus resulted from the release of the ligamentum elasticum interlaminare.
facts.quote: Reisdorf and Wuttke concluded that the death posture indeed resulted from the release of ligaments, more specifically the ligamentum elasticum interlaminare, which spans the spine from the neck to tail in modern birds.

facts.statement: The anaerobic bottom waters of the lagoon likely prevented scavengers from disturbing the Compsognathus carcass before burial.
facts.quote: The bottom water of the lagoon was likely anaerobic (devoid in oxygen), resulting in a sea floor devoid of life except for microbial mats, and therefore preventing scavenging of the carcass.

facts.statement: In 2012, Reisdorf and Wuttke suggested that nodular structures on the fossil slab were remains of adipocere formed by bacteria around the carcass.
facts.quote: Reisdorf and Wuttke, in their 2012 study, suggested that the structures are the remains of adipocere (corpse wax formed by bacteria) that formed around the carcass before burial.

facts.statement: Compsognathus is notable for its small size, which has often been compared to that of a chicken.
facts.quote: For a long time, it was considered unique in its small size, which is commonly compared to that of a chicken.

facts.statement: Compsognathus has appeared in multiple films of the Jurassic Park franchise and the television series Camp Cretaceous and Chaos Theory.
facts.quote: The animals have appeared in the Jurassic Park franchise: in the films The Lost World: Jurassic Park, Jurassic Park III, Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom, Jurassic World Dominion and Jurassic World Rebirth, and the television series Camp Cretaceous and Chaos Theory.

facts.statement: The genus Compsognathus was described by Wagner in 1859.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Wagner, 1859

facts.statement: Compsognathus lived during the Late Jurassic period, approximately 150 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Jurásico Superior, hace 150millones de años, en el Titoniano, en lo que hoy es Europa

facts.statement: Two well-preserved fossils were found, one in Germany in 1850 and a second in France nearly a century later.
facts.quote: Los paleontólogos han encontrado dos fósiles bien preservados, uno en Alemania en 1850 y el segundo en Francia, casi un siglo después

facts.statement: Small, agile lizards preserved in the stomachs of both specimens provide certain evidence of its diet.
facts.quote: los restos de ágiles lagartos pequeños se preservan en los vientres de ambos especímenes

facts.statement: Compsognathus longipes measured around one meter in length.
facts.quote: C.longipes medía alrededor de un metro de longitud

facts.statement: Compsognathus is estimated to have weighed close to 3 kilograms.
facts.quote: Se estima que Compsognathus pesaba cerca de 3kg

facts.statement: Its front limbs were smaller than the hind limbs and equipped with three fingers bearing strong claws adapted for catching prey.
facts.quote: Los miembros delanteros eran más pequeños que los traseros y estaban provistos de garras equipadas con tres dedos de fuertes uñas adaptadas para capturar presas

facts.statement: Its teeth were small but sharp, compatible with a diet of small vertebrates and possibly other small animals like insects.
facts.quote: Los dientes eran pequeños pero afilados, compatibles con su dieta de pequeños vertebrados y posiblemente otros animales pequeños, como insectos

facts.statement: The German specimen presented only two digits on each forelimb, leading scientists to conclude this was the creature's natural state.
facts.quote: El espécimen de Compsognathus descubierto en Alemania en el presentaba solo dos dígitos en cada extremidad anterior

facts.statement: However, the later French fossil revealed the hand had three digits, similar to other compsognathid genera.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, el fósil descubierto más tarde en Francia reveló que la mano tenía tres dígitos, similar a otros miembros de los otros géneros compsognátidos

facts.statement: Bidar hypothesized that the French specimen had palmated hands that would have looked like flippers in life.
facts.quote: Bidar supuso que el espécimen francés tenía manos palmeadas, que se verían como aletas en la vida

facts.statement: L. B. Halstead described the animal as an amphibious dinosaur capable of feeding on aquatic prey and swimming out of reach of large predators.
facts.quote: L. B. Halstead describe al animal como un dinosaurio anfibio capaz de alimentarse de presas acuáticas y de nadar fuera del alcance de los grandes depredadores

facts.statement: Ostrom refuted the amphibious hypothesis by conclusively demonstrating that the French specimen was almost identical to the German one in all aspects except size.
facts.quote: Ostrom desacreditó esta hipótesis al demostrar de manera concluyente que el espécimen francés era casi idéntico al espécimen alemán en todos los aspectos, excepto en su tamaño

facts.statement: Evidence from related species suggests the body may have been covered with feather-like structures.
facts.quote: La evidencia de especies relacionadas sugiere que el cuerpo podría haber estado cubierto con estructuras parecidas a plumas

facts.statement: In 2006, Karin Peyer reported preserved skin impressions on the side of the tail starting at the thirteenth vertebra.
facts.quote: Karin Peyer, en 2006, informó impresiones cutáneas preservadas en el lado de la cola comenzando en la decimotercer vértebra de la cola

facts.statement: The impressions showed small tubercles filled with pits, similar to scales found on the tail and hind legs of Juravenator.
facts.quote: Las impresiones mostraban pequeños tubérculos llenos de baches, similares a las escamas que se encuentran en la cola y las patas traseras de Juravenator

facts.statement: Two nearly complete skeletons are known, one in Germany measuring 85 cm and another in France measuring 155 cm.
facts.quote: A Compsognathus se le conocen dos esqueletos casi completos, uno en Alemania que es de 85 cm de largo, y otro en Francia, de 155 cm

facts.statement: Today, Compsognathus longipes is the only recognized species, although a larger specimen found in France in the 1970s was once thought to represent a separate species, C. corallestris.
facts.quote: Hoy, Compsognathus longipes es la única especie reconocida, aunque se creyó que el espécimen más grande descubierto en Francia en la década de 1970, podía representar una nueva especie separada, C. corallestris

facts.statement: Until the 1990s, Compsognathus was the smallest known dinosaur and the closest known relative of the primitive bird Archaeopteryx.
facts.quote: Hasta la década de1990, Compsognathus era el dinosaurio más pequeño conocido y el pariente conocido más cercano del ave primitiva Archaeopteryx

facts.statement: Compsognathus is classified in the family Compsognathidae.
facts.quote: familia: Compsognathidae

facts.statement: The genus name is Compsognathus.
facts.quote: genus: Compsognathus

facts.statement: Compsognathus longipes means "with elegant jaw and long feet".
facts.quote: Compsognathus longipes ("con mandíbula elegante y pies largos")

facts.statement: The German specimen of Compsognathus was discovered in Bavaria, Germany, during the 1850s by the fossil collector Joseph Oberndorfer.
facts.quote: Joseph Oberndorfer descubrió este fósil de Compsognathus en Baviera, Alemania, en la década de 1850.

facts.statement: Johann A. Wagner first briefly described the specimen in 1859 and formally named it Compsognathus longipes in 1861.
facts.quote: Johann A. Wagner describió al espécimen brevemente en 1859 y de forma más detallada en 1861, cuando utilizó y acuñó el término Compsognathus longipes.

facts.statement: Thomas Huxley hypothesized in 1868 that the specimen was closely related to dinosaurs, and Othniel Marsh confirmed this classification in 1896.
facts.quote: principios de 1868, Thomas Huxley planteó la hipótesis de que el espécimen estuvo estrechamente relacionado con los dinosaurios, y en 1896, Othniel Marsh reconoció al fósil como un auténtico miembro del grupo.

facts.statement: The German holotype specimen is currently housed in the Bavarian State Collection for Palaeontological and Historical Geology in Munich.
facts.quote: El espécimen alemán está en exposición en el Bayerische Staatsammlung für Paläontologie und historische Geologie (Instituto del Estado Bavárico para Paleontología y Geología Histórica), en Múnich, Alemania.

facts.statement: The largest French specimen was discovered in 1972 in the Portland limestone of Canjuers near Nice, France.
facts.quote: El más grande espécimen francés, MNHN CNJ'79, fue descubierto en 1972 en la caliza litográfica de Portland de Canjuers cerca de Niza al sureste de Francia.

facts.statement: The French specimen was acquired by the Muséum national d'histoire naturelle in Paris in 1983 for complete study by Michard.
facts.quote: En 1983, el Muséum national d'histoire naturelle de París, adquirió el fósil del Compsognathus francés, Michard lo estudió ahí completamente.

facts.statement: In 1998, Jens Zinke assigned forty-nine teeth from the Guimarota Formation in Portugal to the genus Compsognathus.
facts.quote: Jens Zinke en 1998 asignó al género cuarenta y nueve dientes de la formación Guimarota del Kimmeridgiense de Portugal.

facts.statement: John Ostrom's thorough redescription in 1978 made Compsognathus one of the best-known small theropods to date.
facts.quote: John Ostrom redescribió la especie a fondo en 1978, haciendo al dinosaurio uno de los terópodos pequeños mejor conocidos hasta la actualidad.

facts.statement: The genus Compsognathus gives its name to the family Compsognathidae, which consists mainly of small dinosaurs from the Late Jurassic and Early Cretaceous of China, Europe, and South America.
facts.quote: Compsognathus le da su nombre a la familia Compsognathidae, un grupo compuesto mayoritariamente por pequeños dinosaurios de finales del Jurásico y comienzos del Cretácico de China, Europa y Sudamérica.

facts.statement: The Compsognathidae clade includes Aristosuchus, Huaxiagnathus, Mirischia, Sinocalliopteryx, Sinosauropteryx, and possibly Juravenator and Scipionyx.
facts.quote: El clado incluye a Aristosuchus, Huaxiagnathus, Mirischia, Sinocalliopteryx, Sinosauropteryx, y tal vez Juravenator y Scipionyx.

facts.statement: Mononykus was initially proposed as a member of the family but was rejected in 1998 as an example of convergent evolution rather than a true relative.
facts.quote: Inicialmente, Mononykus fue propuesto como un miembro de esta familia, pero finalmente fue rechazado por Chen y coautores en un artículo publicado en 1998; consideraron a las similitudes entre Mononykus y los compsognátidos como un ejemplo de evolución convergente.

facts.statement: The position of Compsognathus within Coelurosauria is debated, with some authors arguing it is the most basal coelurosaurian family while others place it within Maniraptora.
facts.quote: La posición del Compsognathus y sus parientes dentro del grupo de celurosaurios es incierta. Algunos autores, como el experto en terópodos Thomas Holtz Jr. y los coautores Ralph Molnar y Phil Currie en el texto del 2004 The Dinosauria, sostienen que la familia es la más ancestral entre los celurosaurios, mientras otros autores defienden que forma parte de Maniraptora.

facts.statement: The Solnhofen limestone deposits, where the German specimen was found, date to the early Tithonian stage.
facts.quote: La piedra caliza del área de Solnhofen ha producido también fósiles bien preservados como Archaeopteryx, con impresiones de plumas, y algunos pterosaurios con marcas de sus membranas alares que datan de la época Titoniense temprana.

facts.statement: The French specimen also dates to the early Tithonian stage.
facts.quote: Data también de comienzos del Titoniense.

facts.statement: Compsognathus lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian stages, approximately 154.8 to 145.06 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (154.8 to 145.06 million years ago)

facts.statement: Remains of a lizard found in the thoracic cavity of the German specimen indicate that Compsognathus fed on small vertebrates.
facts.quote: Los restos de un lagarto en la cavidad torácica del espécimen alemán muestran que este animal se alimentaba de pequeños vertebrados.

facts.statement: Ostrom identified the prey as a Bavarisaurus lizard, and biomechanical simulations suggest Compsognathus was an agile runner capable of reaching speeds near 64 km/h.
facts.quote: Ostrom identificó los restos provenientes de un lagarto del género Bavarisaurus, concluyendo que fue un corredor rápido y ágil debido a su larga cola y a las proporciones de los miembros (según un estudio posterior hecho con simulaciones biomecánicas por Bill Sellers y el paleontólogo Philip Manning llevadas a cabo mediante ordenador en la universidad inglesa de Mánchester y publicado en el boletín Proceedings of the Royal Society, donde aseguran que es el bípedo más rápido hasta ahora conocido, pudiendo alcanzar una velocidad máxima cercana a los 64km/h).

facts.statement: The fact that the Bavarisaurus remains were found in a single piece suggests Compsognathus swallowed its prey whole.
facts.quote: Bavarisaurus está en una sola pieza, indicando que Compsognathus debió haber tragado a su presa entera.

facts.statement: The stomach contents of the French specimen consist of unidentified lizards or sphenodontids.
facts.quote: Los contenidos gástricos del espécimen francés consisten en lagartos o esfenodóntidos sin identificar.

facts.statement: Excavators discovered 10mm diameter eggs near the fossil remains of the German specimen.
facts.quote: Unos excavadores descubrieron huevos de 10mm de diámetro cerca de los restos fósiles del ejemplar alemán.

facts.statement: Later researchers have doubted the assignment of these eggs to Compsognathus because they were found outside the animal's body cavity.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, investigadores posteriores han dudado de su asignación al género porque los encontraron fuera de la cavidad del cuerpo del animal.

facts.statement: The genus name means 'elegant jaw' in Greek, and the species name means 'long legs' in Latin.
facts.quote: El nombre del género proviene del griego kompsos/κομψος, "elegante", "refinado" o "delicado" y gnathos/γναθος; "mandíbula", el de la especie viene del latín y significa "patas largas".

facts.statement: No feathers or similar structures have been preserved in Compsognathus fossils, leading many depictions to show it without feathers.
facts.quote: Ninguna pluma ni estructura similar se ha preservado en fósiles de Compsognathus, en contraste con Archaeopteryx, el cual ha sido hallado en los mismos sedimentos; así, muchas representaciones de Compsognathus lo muestran sin plumas.

facts.statement: Fossils of related genera like Sinosauropteryx show simple feathers covering the body, suggesting Compsognathus likely possessed similar plumage.
facts.quote: Parientes del Compsognathus, como Sinosauropteryx y Sinocalliopteryx, han sido preservados con restos de plumas sencillas cubriendo el cuerpo a modo de pelaje, indicando que Compsognathus debió haber poseído plumaje de manera similar.

facts.statement: The Solnhofen limestone is famous for producing exceptionally well-preserved fossils like Archaeopteryx with feather impressions and pterosaurs with wing membrane marks.
facts.quote: La piedra caliza del área de Solnhofen ha producido también fósiles bien preservados como Archaeopteryx, con impresiones de plumas, y algunos pterosaurios con marcas de sus membranas alares que datan de la época Titoniense temprana.

facts.statement: Quimby identified the smaller German specimen as a juvenile of the same species.
facts.quote: Quimby identificó al espécimen alemán más pequeño como un juvenil de la misma especie.

facts.statement: It is debated whether feather coverage was incomplete in this group, and the family assignment of Juravenator remains uncertain.
facts.quote: Esto puede significar que la cubierta de plumas no era total en este grupo de dinosaurios, aunque una nueva evaluación llevada a cabo por Butler y Upchurch ha puesto en duda la asignación del Juravenator en la misma familia que el compsognato.
